I started with masala papad and shev puri, both of which were crispy and packed with fresh flavors. The shev puri had the perfect balance of tangy chutneys, crunchy puris, and a generous topping of shev, making it a great appetizer.

As a graphic designer, the first thing that caught my attention was the packaging. Every detail feels thoughtfully designed, and it's easily some of the best branding and presentation I've seen in the food space.

The service was equally impressive. The staff was empathetic, kind, and genuinely hospitable, making the entire experience feel warm and welcoming.

Now, the food. The fusions here are absolutely insane in the best way possible. I tried the Chole Bhature Hummus Platter and wow. what a burst of flavours. Bombay Sweet Shop does an incredible job of reimagining familiar Indian flavours in exciting new ways. Between the food, the service, and the beautiful presentation, it's a place I'd happily come back to again and again.

featured_reviews.name: Nikhil Aher
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bombay Sweet Shop – A Modern Take on Traditional Indian Sweets

Bombay Sweet Shop beautifully reimagines Indian mithai with a contemporary twist, both in presentation and flavours. The packaging is premium and festive, making it an excellent choice for gifting—especially during Diwali or special occasions. What stands out is the innovation: classic sweets are thoughtfully reinvented with modern textures, balanced sweetness, and high-quality ingredients.

The variety is impressive, ranging from fusion mithai boxes to snackable treats like barks and savoury options. Each item feels well-crafted and fresh, with consistent quality across products. The store itself is vibrant and inviting, and the staff is helpful when it comes to explaining the concept and recommending combinations.

Pricing is on the higher side compared to traditional sweet shops, but the creativity, hygiene, and overall experience justify it. If you’re looking for something unique that still respects Indian flavours, Bombay Sweet Shop is definitely worth a visit—great for self-indulgence and even better for premium gifting.

featured_reviews.name: Ankur Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
It’s easily one of my absolute favourites in Mumbai! ❤️

From desserts and chocolates to their food and seasonal specials—everything here just hits right. And their coffee? Truly top-notch.

My personal must-tries:
1.	Gymkhana Cold Coffee Softy with Nut Brittle (pro tip: always ask for extra brittle 😉)
2.	Baked Bhatura with Pindi Chole Hummus – those cherry tomatoes, onions & hung curd dip on the side are chef’s kiss 🤌
3.	Veronicas Cold Coffee with oat milk, date syrup & espresso shots – super smooth and perfectly balanced
4.	Fusion Gulab Jamun Churros with Vanilla Dip – and trust me, order a separate pistachio dip… this combo is next level 🤯
5.	Seasonal Desserts – Peach Matcha Cake, Strawberry Tres Leches & more

Honestly, once you try it, it might just become your go-to spot too!

✨ Heads up: Seating is very limited, so be prepared for a short wait or opt for takeaway—totally worth it though!

They also have a great range of souvenirs and healthier options—gluten-free treats, their in-house chikkis (makhana & kurmura), and Indian farsan like bhujia.

✨ Seasonal specials are worth trying too—Ponkh Bhel with Hara Bhara Falafel and Baked Bhatura with Saag Burrata are absolute standouts.

And don’t leave without trying their choco fudge with peanut chikki—it’s to die for! 😍

featured_reviews.review_text:

Perfect for festive celebrations or a special treat, Daab Payesh combines heritage, craftsmanship, and premium ingredients, making it a must-try for anyone seeking authentic Bengali sweets. Sweet Bengal in Bandra West is renowned for maintaining tradition while delivering exceptional quality, making every bite a memorable experience. Indulge in this classic Bengali dessert and discover why it’s celebrated as a quintessential treat for connoisseurs of fine sweets.

featured_reviews.name: Ankur Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re craving indulgent hot or cold chocolate in Mumbai, Chantilly and Chantilly Works, Bandra is an absolute must-visit.

They serve one of the best strawberry chocolates and hot/cold chocolates the city has to offer. It’s clearly a favorite among many—and honestly, I completely get why.

Yes, it may seem a bit pricey at first, but the quality and experience make it totally worth it. I’d highly recommend trying their 75% dark chocolate version—rich, intense, and perfectly balanced.

A little personal ritual I swear by:
I usually order a hot chocolate, enjoy half there, and take the rest home. Refrigerate it overnight and have it cold the next day—it tastes incredible!

One thing to note: the seating space is very small—just a few tables. If you visit at night, be prepared for a wait, even for takeaway sometimes.

I’m not even a big chocolate person, but this place is an exception I happily make.

Must visit when your chocolate cravings hit! 🍫

The presentation is stunning, the quality is consistent, and you can tell a lot of care goes into what they serve. Pair that with a cozy ambience and warm service, and it becomes a place you’ll want to keep coming back to.

If strawberries are your thing, Chantilly – The Café is definitely worth the visit. Highly recommended!

Tharu mithai is the real deal, you can literally taste the ghee and all the mithai is fresh and tastes delish. I've ordered a variety of their sweets- motichoor laddoo, kesar katli, besan laddoo, sohan halwa, mahn ka laddoo and some others that I liked the description of but I forget their names 😂
My only issue is that their online ordering is a bit slow and won't accept international debit cards or even the Indian Bank cards. I had to use my aunt's Indian Bank account to do an online direct transfer.

featured_reviews.name: Jianna Thakur
featured_reviews.review_text:
Its always been a favorite amongst my family. They have the best of Pure Ghee Sweets.. around here. Its gotten even better since a few years now. They have airconditioned their shop... and their level of hygeine has gone up tremendously too. Sweet and Savoury... all their goodies are great.. but do note that.. the prices are steep too.
The Dal Pakhwan is to die for.. seriously scrumptious..!!
And then their Alu Tikki and chholey is yum too.
Been there since so many years now... but this was the first time that I tasted.. and then bought Mysuru Paak. Its simply the melt in the mouth variant. I have tried it at so many South Indian and Maharashtrian sweet shops... but this is by far the best I've had till date.

Must mention Motichoor Laddoo too. After having the laddoo from regular local mishtaan bhandars here... I had started to hate it.
But Tharu's laddoo.. took me back in time.. straight to the halwai shops at Chowk in Allahabad.. now.. Prayagraj. Fried in Pure ghee and steeped in syrup.. yet one can feel each boondi coming apart in every bite. Rarely does one come across.. such perfectly made laddoos nowadays. Well Tharu's motichoor ladoo.. was almost there. Real Motichoor..!!
You must try.. if you havent already.

Must keep something for my next review. So adieu folks. More after my next visit there..

featured_reviews.name: Sagar Gaikwad
featured_reviews.review_text: Yesterday, we ordered 90 pieces of samosas from here, and to our shock, we found small pebbles inside the samosas. We complained about this to the staff, but they were not ready to give any reply. This is very unprofessional, and they are playing with human health. What if a pebble got stuck in someone’s organ? Very bad.

featured_reviews.name: Thedeepseaman Shaun
featured_reviews.review_text: Great place for mithai.. kaju katris are the best. They pack well. For long travel then even shrink wrap and give the boxes. Only issue is the road parking .. always right . Not very cheap but remember

featured_reviews.name: WANDERING SOUL
featured_reviews.review_text: Delicious quality of sweets. Little expensive. But quality wise superb. You can eat samosa and kachori in shop.

featured_reviews.name: Sunil Colaco
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ordered for motichur Laddu received them with fungus.
Ordered dry fruit shrikand this too is not proper. Plz beware before giving sweets to children
Surprisingly the shop agreed the Laddu were spoilt but have still not refunded nor replaced the product

featured_reviews.name: Harish Keswani
featured_reviews.review_text: Best place to purchase Mithais for Gifting. Super quality and taste with attractive gift boxs. Specially recommended Kaju Katli, and many dry fruit mithai with better shelf life than milk based barfis.
